record.original_question: Does there exist a C*-algebra that is approximately amenable but not amenable? If such C*-algebras exist, how can approximate amenability be characterized within the class of C*-algebras?

evidence.quote: From Theorem 2.7, for a general C*-algebra, approximate amenability is the same as pseudo-amenability since it has a bounded approximate identity.
Question 17. Is there an approximately amenable but not amenable C*-algebra? If yes, how to characterize approximate amenability for a C* algebra?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a Banach algebra. A continuous derivation $D: A \to X$ into a Banach $A$-bimodule $X$ is called approximately inner if there exists a net $(\xi_\alpha) \subset X$ such that $D(a) = \lim_\alpha (a \cdot \xi_\alpha - \xi_\alpha \cdot a)$ in norm for every $a \in A$. The Banach algebra $A$ is called approximately amenable if for every Banach $A$-bimodule $X$, every continuous derivation $D: A \to X^*$ (where $X^*$ is the dual bimodule) is approximately inner. The Banach algebra $A$ is called amenable if every such derivation is inner, i.e., of the form $D(a) = a \cdot \xi - \xi \cdot a$ for some fixed $\xi \in X^*$.

Recall that a C*-algebra is a Banach $*$-algebra satisfying $\|a^*a\| = \|a\|^2$, and that every C*-algebra possesses a bounded approximate identity.

(a) Does there exist a C*-algebra $A$ that is approximately amenable but not amenable?

(b) Provide an intrinsic characterization of approximate amenability within the class of C*-algebras: that is, identify a structural property $P$ of C*-algebras such that a C*-algebra $A$ is approximately amenable if and only if $A$ has property $P$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface the foundational papers of Ghahramani–Loy–Zhang on approximate and pseudo-amenability and Haagerup's theorem that for C*-algebras nuclearity is equivalent to amenability, but no source located explicitly settles whether every approximately amenable C*-algebra is amenable, nor provides an intrinsic structural characterization of approximate amenability for C*-algebras. The status of the question therefore appears unresolved in the readily available literature.

status_evidence.title: All nuclear C*-algebras are amenable (Haagerup)
status_evidence.snippet: Haagerup proved that all nuclear C*-algebras are amenable; combined with the converse this gives nuclearity ⇔ amenability for C*-algebras.
status_evidence.claim: For C*-algebras amenability coincides with nuclearity, but this does not address approximate amenability.

status_evidence.title: Approximate and pseudo-amenability of various classes of Banach algebras (Choi–Ghahramani)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of approximate and pseudo-amenability for various Banach algebras following Ghahramani–Loy.
status_evidence.claim: The general theory of approximate amenability is developed, but no characterization specific to C*-algebras is asserted.

status_evidence.title: Bounded pseudo-amenability and contractibility
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses pseudo-amenability and bounded approximate identities; for algebras with a bounded approximate identity, approximate amenability and pseudo-amenability are linked.
status_evidence.claim: Since C*-algebras have bounded approximate identities, approximate amenability and pseudo-amenability coincide there, but neither is shown equivalent to amenability.
